description: Verify the Destination IP Address field of DUT's emitted ARP Request equals the resolution target IPv4 — names the peer whose MAC the DUT is asking for (RFC 826 packet generation)
approach:
[Objective]
The target_ip field of an ARP Request asks 'who has this address?'. It must equal the actual IP DUT is trying to send to — anything else means DUT resolved the wrong peer. This case provokes a DUT ARP Request for HOST-1-IP and asserts the target_ip.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. (No cache seeding — DUT's cache for HOST-1-IP starts empty.)

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message
   ⇒ DUT unicast-Nacks back to HOST-1-IP; cache miss forces an ARP Request to resolve HOST-1-IP.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request
      - opcode      == 1
      - sender_mac  == DUT iface MAC
      - target_ip   == HOST-1-IP   ← key check

[Pass condition]
The observed ARP Request's target_ip equals HOST-1-IP (the destination DUT was asked to reach).

[Fail condition]
• Fail_target_ip — ARP Request seen but target_ip was not HOST-1-IP (DUT resolved the wrong peer — likely a routing/gateway substitution)
• Fail_timeout — No DUT ARP Request observed within the window

verdicts.Pass: ARP Request target_ip matched HOST-1-IP — normal
verdicts.Fail_target_ip: ARP Request emitted but target_ip was not HOST-1-IP — wrong resolution target
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT ARP Request observed within the window
